summary: Jesus warns His disciples against causing others to stumble, commands them to forgive again and again, answers their plea for more faith, and teaches that servants simply do their duty.
key_insight: The apostles asked for more faith right after Jesus told them to forgive a brother seven times in one day. Jesus answered that the size of their faith was not the problem, and that forgiving is not a heroic achievement. It is a servant’s duty.
story: Jesus turned to His disciples. “It is impossible that no offenses should come, but woe to him through whom they do come!” It would be better for that person to be thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

“Take heed to yourselves,” He said. “If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.” Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day comes back saying, ‘I repent,’ “you shall forgive him.”

The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.” He answered, “If you have faith as a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be pulled up by the roots and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.”

Then He asked them to picture a servant coming in from plowing or tending sheep. Would his master say to him, “Come at once and sit down to eat”? No, he would say, “Prepare something for my supper, and gird yourself and serve me till I have eaten and drunk, and afterward you will eat and drink.” Does the master thank the servant for doing what he was told? “I think not.”
“So likewise you, when you have done all those things which you are commanded, say, ‘We are unprofitable servants. We have done what was our duty to do.’”

scene.label: Offenses
scene.text: The word means a snare or a stumbling block, something that trips a person and makes him fall. Jesus is speaking of leading a weaker believer into sin or away from faith.

scene.label: Rebuke, then forgive
scene.text: The Law joined the two long before: “You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him” (Leviticus 19:17), in the same passage that commands love for one’s neighbor. Jesus does not ask His people to pretend sin did not happen.

scene.label: Seven times in a day
scene.text: Seven was the number of completeness. A brother who wrongs you seven times in one day and repents each time would test anyone’s trust, yet Jesus says, “you shall forgive him.” Matthew records a similar word on another occasion: “up to seventy times seven” (Matthew 18:22).

scene.label: The mulberry tree
scene.text: Luke’s word is the sycamine, the black mulberry, a tree known for its strong roots. A tree uprooted and planted in the sea is a picture of the impossible. Elsewhere Jesus speaks of moving a mountain (Matthew 17:20).

scene.label: One servant for everything
scene.text: A small farmer might keep one servant who plowed or herded by day and served at table by evening. “Gird yourself” meant tucking up the long outer robe to work. No one expected a master to thank a servant for a normal day’s work.

witnesses.luke: Luke alone gathers these four sayings together on the road to Jerusalem. Matthew records similar words about stumbling blocks and forgiveness in another setting (Matthew 18:6–7, 21–22). Luke turns from the Pharisees of chapter 16 to the apostles themselves and preserves their short prayer, “Increase our faith.”

seeing.reveals: Jesus guards His little ones fiercely and calls His people to forgive as readily as they rebuke. The Lord who says here that servants earn no thanks is the same Lord who promises, at His coming, to gird Himself and serve His watching servants (Luke 12:37).
seeing.living: You will not forgive a brother seven times in a day by first growing a bigger faith. Faith as small as a mustard seed, resting on God, is enough to begin. And when you have forgiven, do not count it as credit; it is what servants of this Master owe.
seeing.ponder: Whom have you stopped forgiving because you felt you had already done more than enough?

preaching.big_idea: Faithful servants forgive again and again, and claim no credit for it.
outline: Do not trip a little one (1–2)
Rebuke and forgive, again and again (3–4)
Faith as small as a seed (5–6)
preaching.watch_for: The apostles’ prayer in verse 5 is the hinge. It answers the hard command to forgive (vv. 3–4), and Jesus’ reply moves from the power of small faith (v. 6) to the humility of the servant (vv. 7–10).

title: Faith, Forgiveness and Duty
